switches.name: Cognitive continuity resume
switches.explanation: After a restart, resume from the cognitive snapshot - what JARVIS was thinking (intent, chosen plan, beliefs) - not just the goals it had committed to. OFF (default): commitment-only continuity. Safe to enable.

switches.name: Multi-agent orchestration
switches.explanation: The kernel is the authority source for delegated sub-agents - it can only narrow a sub-agent's tools, never widen them, and vetoes a spawn it refuses. Turn OFF to revert to the pre-kernel delegation path.

switches.name: Knowledge-graph recall
switches.explanation: Serve the knowledge prompt block from the typed knowledge graph. Fail-safe: any failure falls back to flat recall. Turn OFF to revert to plain flat recall.

switches.name: Capability authority
switches.explanation: Enforce capability authority on actuating tools - the max-restriction belt, allowlist and kill-switch that stop an un-authorized action. ON (default) is the safe state; OFF reverts to parity (log-only).

switches.name: Autonomy budget ceiling
switches.explanation: Block autonomous actions that exceed the configured budget ceiling. ON (default) is the safe state; OFF reverts to shadow (log-only).

switches.name: Loop / thrash suppression
switches.explanation: Suppress thrashing or looping autonomous actuations. ON (default) is the safe state; OFF reverts to shadow.

switches.name: Safety actuator seam
switches.explanation: Route safety-critical actuators through the policy-mode seam so the active mode's restrictions always apply. ON (default) is the safe state.

switches.name: Freeze-hazard verdict
switches.explanation: Let the kernel own the freeze-hazard verdict (it fails TOWARD alerting). ON (default) is the safe state.

switches.name: Intrusion verdict
switches.explanation: Let the kernel own the intrusion verdict used to arm/alert. ON (default) is the safe state; OFF reverts to the legacy path.

switches.name: Delivery presence verdict
switches.explanation: Let the kernel own per-camera delivery presence. ON (default) is the current behaviour; OFF reverts to the legacy per-camera flag.
